clue.text: That should get the swine clean? Rubbish!

definitions.text: That should get the swine clean?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a wash for a hog would clean a pig
an exclamation dismissing something as nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: a pig (hog) and a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a common term for nonsense or worthless talk, so it serves as an exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Tedious drone with instrument

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A dull droning noise accompanied by some musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monotonous and dull is described as humdrum; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Appear more buoyant having forced the plug in

indicators.note: the words are forced into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone seems more cheerful after forcing a plug into its socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buoyant' suggests floating, but here it means cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer up and become less gloomy is an idiom meaning to seem more cheerful, i.e. buoyant in mood.

clue.text: Tinker reported in US city

indicators.note: reported speech is something said, so the word for tinker is heard rather than written

parts.note: to tinker with something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: A tinker was reported to be living in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like the noun for a travelling mender, but it is the verb meaning meddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Heavyweight Australian boxer covering a crack in my pants!

indicators.note: the Australian creature wraps around the rest, covering it

parts.note: a kangaroo (roo) is famous for boxing with its forelegs

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: A big Australian fighter whose trousers hide a crack, exclamation and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) mixes the letters of 'a crack in my'. 'boxer' seems to belong with 'Heavyweight' but goes with 'Australian': a kangaroo that boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was the undefeated American world heavyweight boxing champion of the 1950s.

clue.text: Holder is cutting the pace

indicators.note: the small word cuts into the gait word, splitting it in two

parts.note: a canter is a horse's pace between trot and gallop

explanation.surface: A holder is cutting the pace of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, something that holds things such as tea or film.

clue.text: Human right to receive support, ultimately

indicators.note: the word for right takes in another letter, receiving it

parts.note: moral means ethically right

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Humanity has a right to receive support in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' tempts as R, but it is the adjective MORAL; the final T of 'support' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human being, subject to death, as opposed to a god.

clue.text: Comment on holy book

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
the Gospel of Mark is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Commentary on a holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Inventor Sir Henry bitter about backfiring shambles

indicators.note: the beer goes round the other piece

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer

indicators.note: backfiring sends the word back the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: a shambles is a mess

explanation.surface: An inventor's bitter complaint about a plan going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns the word for shambles round before it goes inside. Bitter is a hoppy British ale, so 'bitter' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Bessemer invented the Bessemer process for mass-producing steel.

clue.text: Literary idler requiring a fillip when about to marry wife after hesitation

indicators.note: the fillip goes about the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: a fillip is a booster, something that gives a lift

indicators.note: the marrying and wife come after the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
to tie the knot is to marry

explanation.surface: An idle character needs a lift before he will marry after some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is the idle young gentleman of P. G. Wodehouse's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster is the archetypal idle rich young man in English comic fiction.

clue.text: In monogram, a tiny inscription on an old violin?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tiny monogram is inscribed on an antique violin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the maker's label inside an old violin may bear this family name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made famous violins, whose labels carry the maker's name.

clue.text: Pub worker, tattoo possibly etched into knee, say?

indicators.note: a tattoo is etched into the skin, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a knee is an example of something that bends, a bender
a tattoo is a form of body art

explanation.surface: A barman has a tattoo etched into his knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind the bar of a pub; a pub worker.

clue.text: Current man on the board

definitions.meaning: a current of air through a room
a piece in the British board game also known as checkers

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the game checkers is called draughts, and each piece is a draught.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a flow of air and also a counter in the board game draughts.

clue.text: Old king and old cardinal taught

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, an Egyptian pharaoh
cardinal is a deep red colour, from the cardinals' robes

explanation.surface: An old king and an old cardinal taught someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tutored is to be taught, especially privately by a tutor.

clue.text: Incredibly large person shortly having a dance

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: the Incredible Hulk is a huge comic-book character

explanation.surface: A huge person briefly takes part in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The hula is a Hawaiian dance with swaying hips.

clue.text: Cosmonaut finding silence a feature of Saturn? Not quite

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: not quite means not complete, losing the final letter

parts.note: Saturn is known for its rings

explanation.surface: A space traveller silenced by something close to a ring of Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin, a Soviet cosmonaut, was the first human in space in 1961.

clue.text: Greek prison for Rochester's wife?

definitions.meaning: relating to Athens or ancient Greece
in Jane Eyre, Mr Rochester's mad wife Bertha is locked in the top floor of the house

explanation.walkthrough: Rochester is not the Kent town but the hero of Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means Athenian, and a loft room is where Bertha Mason was confined.

clue.text: Darling expected, it's said, saccharine stuff

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like darling

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for expected is taken by sound

parts.note: something due is expected

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is said to be expected, bringing something sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeydew is the sweet sticky secretion of aphids, also a sweet melon, so sugary stuff.

clue.text: Scorcher taking in Bobby, cool dude

indicators.note: the heat takes the policeman in, surrounding him

parts.note: a scorcher is a very hot day, i.e. heat
a bobby is a British police officer, a PC (police constable)

explanation.surface: On a scorching day a policeman takes in a cool character.
explanation.definitionFit: A hepcat is old jazz slang for a hip, stylish person.

clue.text: Very little time to pass the ball in sport

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
taken as written
in football to cross is to pass the ball across the field

explanation.surface: In a sport, there is very little time to pass the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Motocross is the sport of off-road motorcycle racing.

clue.text: Fortification hit a bit

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A fortification was hit a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or bank around a fort.

clue.text: A bird me, a nocturnal flier in the night

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the flier goes in the night word

parts.note: night is the dark
the owl flies at night

explanation.surface: A bird speaks: me, a night-flying creature in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is a North American songbird.

clue.text: Match reference book, a record so extraordinarily gripping

indicators.note: the jumbled letters grip the abbreviation, holding it inside
done in an extraordinary way, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference book describes an extraordinary gripping record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' mixes A RECORD SO into SCOREOARD, around B.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard is what spectators consult during a match to see the score.

clue.text: Function of a colander stretched to the limit?

definitions.meaning: a colander drains, sieving liquid from food

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is sieving food; the other is pulling or striving with all one's strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining is both sieving out liquid and making a great effort, stretching oneself.

clue.text: Politician right to punch purring protester?

indicators.note: the letter punches into the other piece, ending up inside

parts.note: playfully, a cat (purring) at a demo (protest)

explanation.surface: A right-winger punches a protester who purrs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'purring protester' is a whimsical demo cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, a politician.

clue.text: Instrument adopted by mother, a sorceress

indicators.note: the instrument is taken in by mother, adopted into her

parts.note: ma is mother
an organ is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: An instrument taken on by mother, a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: Morgan le Fay, or Morgana, is the enchantress of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Morgana is the sorceress Morgan le Fay of the King Arthur stories.

clue.text: Stick a border up for a high window

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters run upward, in reverse

parts.note: a rod is a stick
a rim is a border

explanation.surface: Fixing a border up high for a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a turret or balcony window with a view, typical of Spanish architecture.

clue.text: In America, petty idiot constrains our British leaders

indicators.note: the idiot constrains the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a twit is an idiot

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: In America an idiot constrains the British, petty-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is American slang meaning cheap or insignificant, i.e. petty.

clue.text: With a minimum of tact, little time for message?

indicators.note: the least possible of the word, its first letter

parts.note: wee means little

explanation.surface: With very little tact, briefly sending a message.
explanation.walkthrough: A tweet is a short message posted on Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short social-media post, a message.

clue.text: Conventional missile sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile

explanation.surface: A conventional missile was launched upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional, i.e. conventional, as in trad jazz.
